retrieved_context.text_excerpt: Composite supply means a supply consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business. The tax liability shall be determined as if the supply were that of the principal supply.

Mixed supply means two or more individual supplies made together for a single price where such supply does not constitute a composite supply. Tax liability for mixed supply is treated as supply attracting highest rate of tax.

generated_mcqs.subject: Indirect Tax Laws (IDT)
generated_mcqs.question_statement: A supplier offers air-conditioner installation bundled with mandatory stabilizer and standard installation for a single price. Which GST characterization is most accurate based on naturally bundled principles?

options.label: A
options.text: Composite supply taxable at the rate applicable to principal supply.

options.label: B
options.text: Mixed supply taxable at the highest rate among all supplied items.

options.label: C
options.text: Exempt supply because installation is ancillary to goods.

options.label: D
options.text: Two independent supplies to be taxed separately even if naturally bundled.

generated_mcqs.correct_explanation: Where supplies are naturally bundled in ordinary course and one is principal, classification is composite supply and tax follows principal supply.

distractor_explanations.B: Highest-rate rule applies to mixed supply, not naturally bundled composite supply.
distractor_explanations.C: No exemption follows merely because one element is ancillary.
distractor_explanations.D: Naturally bundled supplies are not split for separate taxation in this context.

source_reference.excerpt: Composite supply ... naturally bundled ... tax liability as principal supply.

generated_mcqs.question_statement: Gift hamper containing unrelated items sold for one consolidated festive price, without natural bundling, should be treated as:

options.label: A
options.text: Composite supply taxed at principal supply rate.

options.label: B
options.text: Mixed supply taxed at highest applicable rate among items.

options.label: C
options.text: Non-taxable transaction due to bundled pricing.

options.label: D
options.text: Supply of goods only taxed at average rate.

generated_mcqs.correct_explanation: Unrelated items supplied together for a single price without natural bundling are mixed supply and tax follows highest-rate item.

distractor_explanations.A: Composite supply needs natural bundling and principal supply identification.
distractor_explanations.C: Bundled pricing does not convert taxable supply into non-taxable transaction.
distractor_explanations.D: GST does not prescribe averaging rates for mixed supply classification.

source_reference.excerpt: Mixed supply ... does not constitute composite supply ... highest rate of tax.
